title: Single decorative street lamp
prompt: Make me a nice old-fashioned street lamp I can copy around my town.

good: Readable silhouette at a glance: base plinth, tapered post, arm or crossbar, lantern head with a cap — at least four distinguishable segments, not one stretched cylinder.
Lantern housing is built from more than a single part: a glass/neon panel inset inside a darker frame, with a finial or cap on top.
Post reads roughly 2.5x-3.5x a Roblox character in height (about 12-18 studs) so it is believable at human scale.
Metal parts use a metal-family material (Metal, DiamondPlate, CorrodedMetal, Slate) while the light element is Neon or Glass — material tells you what the thing is made of.
A PointLight or SpotLight is actually parented under the lantern, and its colour agrees with the Neon part's colour.
Small trim details under 2 studs exist: bolts, a collar where the arm meets the post, a base ring.
bad: One grey cylinder with a yellow ball on top — the current Golem failure mode.
Lantern is a bare Neon sphere with no housing or frame.
Post is 40 studs tall or 3 studs tall — no human scale reference.
Everything is Plastic with SmoothPlastic-default colours.
No light source instance at all, so at night it is a dark pole.
Zero parts smaller than 2 studs — no trim, no bolts, no collar.

notes: The whole scene IS the prop, so composition and spatial-flow weights are dialled down and silhouette/trim are dialled up.

title: Single furnished room interior
prompt: Build a cozy bedroom for my roleplay game — bed, desk, wardrobe, a window, that kind of thing.

good: Room has a floor, four walls and a ceiling with a real doorway and a real window opening — not a floating rug with furniture on it.
Walls carry a skirting board and either a cornice or a picture rail; the window has a frame and sill, the door has a jamb.
Bed is a stack of parts (frame, mattress, duvet, two pillows, headboard) with the mattress inset from the frame, not one brown block.
Furniture is at plausible human scale: bed about 6x10 studs, desk surface at about 3 studs off the floor, wardrobe about 9 studs tall.
Three layers of stuff: architecture (walls/floor), furniture (bed/desk/wardrobe), and clutter (a lamp, books, a mug, a rug, a poster).
Warm interior lighting: a PointLight in the room, Lighting.Ambient/OutdoorAmbient nudged warm, and window light justified by a bright exterior.
Wood-family materials on furniture, fabric-family on bed and rug, and a distinct wall material — at least four materials in the room.
bad: Four flat walls of the same grey Plastic, one brown box for a bed, one brown box for a desk.
Window is a blue-tinted part flush with the wall with no frame, or there is no window at all despite the prompt.
No skirting or trim anywhere — every wall/floor junction is a raw 90-degree seam.
Furniture floats above the floor or clips through walls.
Zero clutter props: the room is architecture plus three boxes and reads empty.
Default lighting untouched, so the interior is lit exactly like the outdoors.

notes: The bed is the focal point; graders should be able to name it from the hero shot.

title: Outdoor town plaza hub
prompt: I need a town square for the middle of my game where players hang out — make it look welcoming.
heroObject: the centrepiece (fountain, clock tower or statue)

good: A single unmistakable centrepiece (fountain, clock tower, statue) that is taller than everything around it and sits at a deliberate point — centre or a third — not lost in the middle of a grid.
Ground is a paved surface with a pattern: an inlaid ring or radial banding around the centrepiece, a border course, and a different material for planting beds.
Perimeter is defined — benches, planters, low walls, lamp posts, or building facades — so the plaza reads as a room outdoors rather than a slab in a void.
Clear circulation: readable paths in and out, and open floor kept clear near the centrepiece so it has breathing room.
Height stepping: ground plane, bench/planter height (about 2-4 studs), lamp/tree height (about 12-18 studs), centrepiece tallest.
Trees or planting with more than one part per tree (trunk plus at least two canopy volumes at different heights).
bad: A flat square baseplate-coloured slab with objects scattered evenly across it in a grid.
Centrepiece is the same height as the benches, or there is no centrepiece at all.
Ground is one unmodified material and one colour edge to edge.
Props hug the outer edge with a dead empty middle, or the middle is so cluttered you cannot walk through.
Trees are a brown cylinder with a green sphere.
Everything at exactly the same height so the top-down and eye views look identical in information.

notes: Highest-signal task for composition and negative space. If a scene fails here it will fail in front of a real player.

title: Obby course section
prompt: Add the next section of my obby — about 8 jumps, medium difficulty, make it look like a lava level.
heroObject: the route itself (start pad to end pad)

good: Reads as a route: you can trace start to end in the top view, and gaps are jumpable (roughly 6-14 studs at the same height, shorter when climbing).
Vertical progression — the course climbs or descends, so the side view is a legible profile rather than a flat line of identical pads.

Lava theme carried through: hot emissive material (Neon/Glowing orange) for hazard surfaces, darkened charred rock (Basalt/Slate/CorrodedMetal) for safe platforms, so hazard vs safe is readable by colour alone.
Platform shapes vary — different sizes, a moving/rotating one, a narrow beam, a wider rest pad — instead of eight identical cubes.
Hazard surfaces are visually hot: emissive colour plus a light or particle, not just a red-tinted Plastic block.
Every platform anchored, checkpoints or a visible safe landing at the end.
bad: Eight identical grey blocks in a straight line at one height.
Gaps that are not jumpable (over about 20 studs) or so small they are not jumps.
Lava is a flat red Plastic part with no glow and no light.
Safe and hazard surfaces are the same colour family so a player cannot read danger.
Platforms unanchored so the course collapses on play.
No sense of direction — platforms scattered with no traceable route.

notes: Landmark is not required; the route itself is the subject. Focal point is scored on whether the route start/end reads, not on a statue.

title: Market vendor stall
prompt: Make a little market stall where an NPC sells potions.
heroObject: the stall counter with its potion display

good: Stall structure has corner posts, a counter, a back shelf and a canopy or awning — a real three-dimensional structure with a front and a back.
Awning is striped or panelled (alternating colour parts), sagging or angled rather than a flat rectangle floating on top.
The counter is dressed: potion bottles of varying heights, a crate, a sign, a till, a lantern. At least eight small props under 2 studs.
Potions read as potions: small Glass/Neon bodies with a darker cork, and more than one colour so they read as different items.
Wood posts and counter, fabric canopy, glass bottles, stone or dirt ground under the stall — materials tell the story.
Human scale: counter about 3.5 studs high, canopy clearing a character's head at about 8-10 studs.
bad: A table-shaped block with a flat rectangle floating above it as the roof.
Awning is one solid colour with no stripe, panel or fold.
Bottles are identical cylinders in one colour, or absent entirely despite 'sells potions'.
Whole stall is one wood colour with no trim, no counter lip, no post caps.
Fewer than three small props — the counter is bare.
Canopy at 4 studs so a character could not stand under it.

notes: Highest-signal task for surface-detail density and prop layering: the shape is easy, the dressing is where scenes fail.

title: Spawn / lobby area
prompt: Build the spawn area for my game — somewhere players land when they join and can see where to go.
heroObject: the spawn dais and the exit it points to

good: SpawnLocation(s) are visually integrated — a raised dais, a pad with a border ring, or a marked circle — not a naked blue-and-white default part sitting on the floor.
The exit is legible from the spawn point: an arch, a gate, a lit path, or a sightline that tells you where to walk.
Framed space: walls, pillars, or a canopy give the area edges, so a player who just joined understands the room.
Ground reads as designed floor: an inlay, a border, a change of material at the threshold.
Deliberate lighting — the exit or the dais is brighter than the surrounds so the eye is led.
Some welcome dressing: banners, planters, a sign, seating — at least three prop types beyond the architecture.
bad: Default SpawnLocation dropped on a bare baseplate with nothing around it.
No indication of where to go — a symmetric empty box with no exit emphasis.
Ground is the unmodified baseplate, still showing its default studs/colour.
All-uniform lighting so nothing draws the eye.
Walls with no openings, or openings with no frames.
Zero dressing props.

notes: The 'ground is still an unmodified baseplate' hard fail is most likely to fire here; that is intentional.

title: Natural landscape vignette
prompt: Make a peaceful forest clearing with a little stream running through it.

good: Ground is irregular: sculpted terrain or varied parts with grass, dirt patches, rock outcrops and a bank down to the stream — never a flat green rectangle.
Stream has banks, a bed under the water, stones in or beside it, and a water-family material (Water/Glass/Ice) with transparency, not a flat blue Plastic ribbon.
Trees are built: trunk, at least two branches or a tapered trunk, and three or more canopy volumes at different heights and slightly different greens.
Green palette is disciplined — three to five related greens plus browns, not six unrelated saturated hues.
Value structure reads: dark trunks and shadowed undergrowth against lighter canopy and open clearing floor.
Atmosphere set: Lighting ClockTime/Brightness tuned, Atmosphere or FogEnd used, and light colour warmed so the clearing feels like a time of day.
The clearing itself is kept open — negative space in the middle is doing work, with density around the edges.
bad: Flat green rectangle for the ground with a flat blue rectangle laid on top as the stream.
Trees are one cylinder plus one sphere, all identical, evenly spaced.
Grass green is the default bright Roblox green, unrelated to the canopy green.
No terrain height variation whatsoever — the side view is a straight line.
Default Lighting: noon-white, no fog, no atmosphere, so it looks like a diagram.
Trees fill the clearing evenly so there is no clearing.

notes: Nature scenes fail on palette and value first; a hero tree or rock is welcome but not required.

title: Dungeon corridor
prompt: Give me a dark stone dungeon hallway with torches, leading to a locked door.
heroObject: the locked door at the end of the corridor

good: Corridor has floor, two walls, and a ceiling or arch, with the door as the terminating focal element at the end of the sightline.
Stone is articulated: separate block courses, a differently-sized base course, pilasters or ribs at intervals — not two flat wall slabs.
Torches are real light sources: a bracket, a Neon flame, a PointLight with warm colour and a sensible range, spaced so pools of light and dark alternate along the corridor.
Lighting is actually dark — Ambient/OutdoorAmbient lowered, Brightness reduced, so torchlight reads. The eye view should be dim.
Value structure: bright torch pools, mid-tone lit walls, near-black recesses. Not one flat exposure.
The locked door is distinct from the walls — heavier material, metal banding, a lock/handle prop, and it is the brightest or most contrasted thing at the end.
bad: Two flat grey walls and a flat floor, evenly lit at default brightness — a 'dungeon' at noon.
Torches are orange blocks with no PointLight, so nothing is actually lit.
Lighting properties untouched, so the corridor is as bright as the outdoors.
Door is the same grey block as the wall with no banding, lock or trim.
No ceiling, so the corridor reads as an outdoor trench.
Uniform texture across every surface with no course lines, ribs or wear.

notes: Best task for the default-lighting hard fail. A corridor that is bright is wrong no matter how many parts exist.

title: Battle arena / stadium
prompt: Build a battle arena for PvP — fighting floor in the middle with seating around it.
heroObject: the fighting floor at the centre of the bowl

good: Clear three-zone read: fighting floor, a barrier/moat separating it from the stands, and tiered seating that steps upward.
Seating is genuinely tiered — at least four rows at increasing height and depth, with an aisle or two cutting through them.
Fighting floor is marked: a centre circle, boundary line, or material change so the combat area is legible from the eye view.
Scale is stadium-scale relative to a character: barrier about 5-8 studs, top of the stands 25+ studs, floor wide enough to fight in (40+ studs).
Structural language repeats — pillars, arches or buttresses at a consistent rhythm around the bowl, giving a readable silhouette from outside.
Something above the rim: banners, floodlights, a scoreboard, or a partial roof, so the top view is not just a flat ring.
bad: A flat circle with a ring of blocks around it at one height.
Seating is a single sloped ramp with no individual rows.
No barrier between fighters and spectators.
Arena floor the same material and colour as the seating and the surrounding ground.
Pillars placed at irregular arbitrary intervals with no rhythm.
Everything under 8 studs tall so the top view and side view carry the same information.

notes: Tests whether the builder can hold a large composition together; scale errors show up brutally in the eye view.

title: Large hero prop — pirate ship
prompt: Build a pirate ship for my island map — it doesn't have to drive, it's a set piece.
heroObject: the ship's hull and mast silhouette

good: Silhouette is unmistakably a ship from the side view: a hull that tapers at bow and stern, a raised stern castle, masts of differing heights, a bowsprit.
Hull is planked or ribbed — repeated horizontal strakes and vertical ribs — not one scaled box or wedge.
Rigging present: at least masts, a crossyard per mast, and sails as thin angled parts, plus some line/rope parts.
Deck is dressed: railings with individual balusters, hatches, barrels, crates, a wheel, a lantern. Ten or more small props.
Scale believable against a character: deck railing about 3.5 studs, main mast 30-50 studs, hull long enough to walk (50+ studs).
Materials tell material: Wood/WoodPlanks hull and deck, Fabric sails, Metal fittings, rope in a distinct brown.
bad: A brown wedge with two grey cylinders sticking out of it.
Hull is a single stretched part with no planking, ribs or curvature suggestion.
Sails are opaque flat rectangles in default white, or absent.
Deck is empty — no railings, no barrels, no wheel.
Masts identical in height and thickness, spaced evenly.
Whole ship one flat brown colour in one material.

notes: Silhouette-dominant. If the top and side views do not read as a ship, no amount of part count rescues it.

title: In-world signage and wayfinding
prompt: Put up a big sign at the entrance to my shop area that says SHOPS, plus arrows pointing to the different stores.

good: Sign has a structure: posts or an arch frame, a backing board with a border/bezel, and the lettering surface inset into it.
Text is legible in the eye view at player distance — large enough, high contrast against its backing, and facing the approach.
Arrow signs are shaped like arrows (a pointed plate or a distinct arrow head), not rectangles with the word 'left' on them.
Signage is lit or emissive so it reads at any time of day — a SurfaceLight, Neon backing, or a spotlight aimed at the board.
Consistent visual language: the main sign and the arrow signs share materials, border treatment and palette so they read as one system.
Mounted at a sensible height — board centre roughly 8-14 studs, arms clear of a character's head.
bad: A floating flat part with a SurfaceGui and nothing else — no frame, no post, no bezel.
Text tiny or low-contrast so it is unreadable in the eye view.
Arrows are plain rectangles or are missing entirely despite the prompt asking for them.
Sign and arrows use unrelated colours and materials, so they do not read as a set.
Sign sunk into the ground or floating 30 studs in the air.
No emissive or lit treatment, so at dusk the signage disappears.

notes: Prompt fidelity is genuinely load-bearing here (the word SHOPS, the arrows) — but it is still capped at its global weight so a legible-but-ugly sign cannot pass.

title: Polish an existing ugly scene
prompt: This looks really bad. Can you make my cafe look good? Don't move stuff around, just make it look nicer.

good: Same footprint and same object positions as the seed scene — the improvement is finish, not a rebuild.
Every flat grey Plastic surface has been reassigned a purposeful material: WoodPlanks floor, Brick or Concrete walls, Metal fittings, Glass windows.
A coherent palette has been imposed: one dominant neutral, one wood/warm mid tone, one accent colour used sparingly on three or four elements.
Trim added at junctions: skirting where walls meet floor, a counter lip, window frames, a cornice or fascia — the single biggest cheap win.
Lighting reworked: warm interior PointLights, Ambient/OutdoorAmbient adjusted, ClockTime moved off harsh noon.
Small props added on existing surfaces: cups, a menu board, plants, napkin holders — dressing that does not move the furniture.
Existing box furniture broken up with at least one added part each (a table gets a rim, chairs get a back-rail, the counter gets a front panel).
bad: Objects rearranged or replaced instead of finished — violates the explicit 'don't move stuff around'.
Colours changed but every part still Plastic — recolouring is not polishing.
One material swapped globally so the whole cafe is now uniformly Brick.
Saturation cranked: six unrelated bright hues, worse than the grey it replaced.
Lighting untouched, so the same flat noon exposure survives the pass.
No trim added anywhere; every junction is still a raw seam.
Nothing added under 2 studs, so surfaces are still bare.

notes: The purest test of the thesis: object existence is unchanged between before and after, so any score delta is entirely visual quality. Prompt fidelity is de-emphasised because it is trivially satisfied by the seed scene.
